rv.q: Applause has too much heart and is simply too much fun to be bogged down by its shortcomings, so audiences should take advantage of catching this gem while they can.
A great story can survive a merely good score when the actresses behave badly in fabulous clothes, and Applause has both in generous supply.

I applaud Applause , which I’d never seen before. Despite the fact that, with the exception of the vocals, which are indeed performed live, the rest of the soundtrack is a recording (John Harvey is the sound manager), I enjoyed most of the music, as well as the dancing (choreo by Becca Sweitzer) and acting.
The songs themselves are largely mediocre, and the company deserves better than the tinny, pre-recorded soundtrack — the only element that circumvents this almost heroic enterprise.

Applause (like Two Gentlemen of Verona and Raisin) has achieved only obscurity, making the Group Rep staging one that Broadway buffs will want to catch if only to see for themselves why it is almost never revived.

cn.t: The Group Rep's revival delivers strong performances from Stevens and Mortenson, but this 1970s musical adaptation of "All About Eve" remains lesser fare compared to its Tony-winning contemporaries from the era.
